scenes.headline: How a diffusion model loops on its hard tokens
scenes.sub: Amazon's adaptively looped diffusion language model, built from Qwen3
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Spindle! This diffusion language model spends more layers on the tokens it finds hard, inside every denoising step.

scenes.text: Inside one denoising step, confident tokens commit and become context, while unresolved tokens keep their hidden state and loop through the same layers again.
scenes.say: Confident tokens commit and become context. Unresolved tokens keep their hidden state and loop through the same layers again.

left.title: A standard diffusion step
items: Every masked token gets the same depth
Deferred tokens restart from a mask
left.say: A standard diffusion step gives every masked token the same depth, and a deferred token's work is thrown away.

right.title: A looped step
items: The middle layers run up to 4 times
Hard tokens carry their state forward
right.say: Here the middle layers run up to four times, and hard tokens carry their state from pass to pass.

steps.say: The masked window goes through the prelude once.
Then the shared core runs, and after every pass the coda reads out a prediction.
Two heads read each position: the language model head, and a tiny exit gate.
Low-entropy positions commit, and their token embeddings become context.
The rest loop back through the core until the gate's average says stop, or pass four.

scenes.title: Teaching the gate when to stop
scenes.text: sequence cost x log q(exit schedule)
scenes.say: Exits are discrete, so the gate is trained like a policy.

parts.note: loss at the sampled exit, minus the first-pass loss
parts.say: Each sampled schedule gets a cost: the loss where tokens exited, minus the loss after one pass.
That cost scales the schedule's log probability, with a prior favouring shallow exits.

scenes.title: Which pass each token committed on

steps.say: On a real answer, darker means a later pass. Almost nothing commits on the first.
The arithmetic and the boxed answer are mostly pass four.

scenes.title: Average over eleven benchmarks, 8B
scenes.note: one token per pass; Qwen3 never saw the 5B-token fine-tuning corpus
scenes.say: It beats the best diffusion baseline by over five points. The lead over Qwen3 is measured one token per pass, against a parent that never saw its training data.

scenes.text: Keep the work on tokens you aren't ready to commit: looping them inside the step makes a better diffusion model.
scenes.say: So: don't throw away the work on tokens you aren't ready to commit. Loop them.

recap: Middle layers loop up to 4 times per step
Entropy commits tokens, the gate stops the loop
Beats WeDLM clearly; the AR lead needs a control
scenes.say: To recap: the core loops, entropy commits, the gate stops, and the lead over Qwen3 needs a same-data control.
